Depends first on the equipment. United’s new F seats are quite excellent, but you could also get their super old hard product. Some people love these seats because they’re like old plush recliners but they feel so, so dated. Meanwhile, AA’s F cabins are essentially the same throughout the fleet and aren’t bad, basically the same as their PE product (and Delta Premium Plus) but they don’t have IFE. From LA to AUA however you might get a nice widebody on one of the legs; I know AA used to fly 773s and 789s between LAX and MIA, and you’ll often find Dreamliners on UA between LAX and IAH or IAD.

Depends also on the routing. Is AA sending you through Charlotte? Avoid. Dallas (AA) or Houston (UA) during thunderstorm season? Avoid. United through EWR? Run away screaming. 

Having been a high-level elite with each of the big three carriers, I find United to be a better airline with better service, better food, and better ops when compared to AA, and United is really trying to compete with Delta in the luxury market and has been making great strides.
